eli5: One layer of notes about the picture, like one colour layer.
simple: One 2-D grid of numbers in a feature map. A map with 64 channels is 64 stacked grids, each describing a different pattern.
engineer: Size of dimension 1 of an N×C×H×W tensor.

eli5: A picture of notes the model made about the photo.
simple: The output of a layer: a stack of channels, each a grid that says how strongly some pattern appears at each place.

eli5: How many steps the window jumps each time. A jump of 2 makes the picture half as big.
simple: How far a filter moves between positions. Stride 2 halves width and height. A map's stride (8, 16, 32) also says how many input pixels one cell covers.
engineer: Sampling step of a conv/pool; also the cumulative downsampling factor of a pyramid level (P_k has stride 2^k).

eli5: A tiny window of learned numbers that looks for one pattern.
simple: The small grid of learned weights (for example 3×3) that a convolution slides over the map.

eli5: Sliding a small window over the picture and writing down what it sees.
simple: An operation that slides a learned kernel over the input and computes a weighted sum at each position.
engineer: Discrete cross-correlation y = W ∗ x (+ b).

eli5: A helper that mixes the notes at each spot without looking at neighbours.
simple: A convolution with a 1×1 kernel: it only mixes channels at each position. Used to change the number of channels cheaply.
engineer: Pointwise conv; per-pixel linear projection over channels.

eli5: Each layer of notes gets its own small window, which is much cheaper.
simple: A convolution where each channel is filtered separately (groups = channels). Often followed by a 1×1 conv; together called depthwise-separable. Much cheaper than a normal conv.
engineer: Grouped conv with g = c1; depthwise-separable = DW k×k + PW 1×1, cost ≈ 1/c2 + 1/k² of a dense conv.

eli5: Keeps the numbers from getting too big or too small.
simple: Rescales each channel so its values have a steady average and spread during training, which makes learning faster and more stable.
engineer: Per-channel standardisation with learned γ, β and running statistics; fused into conv at inference.

eli5: A rule that decides how much of each note passes on.
simple: A simple function applied to every value after a layer (like SiLU). Without it, stacking layers would add nothing new.
engineer: Elementwise nonlinearity enabling non-linear function approximation.

eli5: A smooth switch: lets good signals through and quiets the rest.
simple: The activation used in YOLO: x × sigmoid(x). Positive values pass almost unchanged, negative ones shrink smoothly toward zero.

eli5: Squashes any number into a value between 0 and 1.
simple: A function that maps any number to the range 0–1, used for probabilities and gates.

eli5: Turns a list of scores into percentages that add up to 100%.
simple: Turns a list of numbers into probabilities that sum to 1; bigger numbers get most of the weight.

eli5: The numbers the model learns. More numbers means a bigger model.
simple: The learned numbers inside the model (kernel weights, batch-norm values). They are what training changes and what the saved file stores.

eli5: How much counting work the model does for one picture.
simple: Floating-point operations: a measure of how much computation one image needs. GFLOPs = billions. Ultralytics counts 2 per multiply-add.
engineer: 2 × MACs (thop convention), at the stated input size.

eli5: How big a part of the photo one spot can 'see'.
simple: The area of the input image that can influence one output cell. Deeper layers and pooling make it bigger.
engineer: Input region contributing to an output activation; grows with depth, kernel size and stride.

eli5: The part that looks at the photo and makes notes.
simple: The first part of the network that turns the image into feature maps at several sizes.
engineer: Hierarchical feature extractor producing multi-scale features.

eli5: The part that mixes notes from different sizes.
simple: The middle part that combines feature maps of different sizes so each has both detail and context.

eli5: The part that makes the final answers.
simple: The last part that turns feature maps into predictions (boxes, classes, masks, keypoints).

eli5: Passes big-picture understanding down to the detailed maps.
simple: Feature Pyramid Network: a top-down path that upsamples deep maps and joins them with shallower ones.
engineer: Top-down pathway with lateral connections (Lin et al., 2017).

eli5: Passes detail back up to the big-picture maps.
simple: Path Aggregation Network: a bottom-up path after FPN that brings fine detail back to the deeper maps.
engineer: Bottom-up augmentation after FPN (Liu et al., 2018).

eli5: The most detailed map used for answers, best for small things.
simple: The pyramid level with stride 8 (80×80 at 640). Used to find small objects.

eli5: The middle map, for medium things.
simple: The pyramid level with stride 16 (40×40 at 640). Used for medium objects.

eli5: The smallest, most meaningful map, for big things.
simple: The pyramid level with stride 32 (20×20 at 640). Used for large objects.

eli5: An extra, very detailed map for tiny things.
simple: An optional level with stride 4 (160×160 at 640). Added for tiny objects; it is much more expensive.

eli5: The model guesses boxes directly, without ready-made box shapes.
simple: Predicts each box as distances from a cell centre to its four sides, instead of adjusting a set of preset box shapes (anchors).
engineer: Point-based box regression without anchor priors.

eli5: A fixed spot on the grid where the model makes a guess.
simple: In YOLOv8+, the centre of each grid cell where a prediction is made (8,400 at 640). Older YOLOs used anchor boxes of preset shapes.
engineer: Grid location (and, historically, prior box shape).

eli5: A clean-up step that removes copies of the same box.
simple: Non-maximum suppression: keeps the best box and removes boxes that overlap it too much.
engineer: Greedy IoU-based suppression of redundant detections.

eli5: How much two boxes overlap, from 0 (not at all) to 1 (exactly the same).
simple: Intersection over union: overlap area divided by the combined area of two boxes.

eli5: A score for how good a detector is, from 0 to 100.
simple: Mean average precision: the standard detection score, averaged over classes (and IoU thresholds 0.5–0.95 for mAP50-95).
engineer: Mean over classes of area under the precision–recall curve, averaged over IoU ∈ [0.5:0.95].

eli5: Of the boxes the model drew, how many were right.
simple: Correct detections divided by all detections.

eli5: Of the real things, how many the model found.
simple: Found objects divided by all real objects.

eli5: 16 little votes for where each box side is.
simple: Distribution Focal Loss: each box side is predicted as a probability over 16 distances, then averaged into one value. Removed in YOLO26.
engineer: GFL-style discretised regression with reg_max bins.

eli5: The teacher that picks which guesses should learn each object.
simple: Task-Aligned Learning assigner: during training, picks the predictions that are good both at the class and at the box for each labelled object.

eli5: A teacher rule that makes sure tiny things also get helpers.
simple: Small-Target-Aware Label Assignment (YOLO26): improves which predictions learn small objects; in Ultralytics' code, tiny boxes are enlarged to the stride size when choosing candidates.
engineer: GT boxes with sides < stride are enlarged for candidate selection in TAL.

eli5: A training plan that slowly shifts attention to the final answers.
simple: Progressive Loss (YOLO26): the weight moves from the one-to-many head toward the one-to-one head as training goes on.
engineer: Linear decay of o2m loss weight (0.8 → 0.1), o2o = 1 − w.

eli5: A way of updating the model's numbers while it learns.
simple: An optimizer used by YOLO26 that combines SGD with Muon, an idea from large language model training.

eli5: Each real thing gets exactly one answer.
simple: A head trained so each object matches exactly one prediction, which removes the need for NMS.
engineer: Top-1 assignment branch enabling NMS-free inference.

eli5: Each real thing gets several helpers while learning.
simple: A head trained so each object matches several predictions; gives strong training signal but needs NMS.

eli5: The model gives final answers by itself, with no clean-up.
simple: A model whose outputs need no NMS: one prediction per object comes straight out of the network.

eli5: Each spot looks at other spots to decide what matters.
simple: A layer where every position computes how much to look at every other position and mixes their information accordingly.

eli5: Attention inside a few big strips of the picture, to save time.
simple: YOLO12's attention that splits the map into a few equal regions (default 4) and runs attention inside each.

eli5: Several attention helpers, each looking for something different.
simple: Attention split into several heads that each attend separately; their results are joined.

eli5: What a spot is looking for.
simple: In attention, the vector a position uses to ask 'who is relevant to me?'.

eli5: How a spot describes itself to others.
simple: In attention, the vector each position offers to be matched against queries.

eli5: The information a spot shares.
simple: In attention, the content that is mixed according to the attention weights.

eli5: A shortcut that adds the input back to the output.
simple: A connection that adds a block's input to its output, so the block only learns a correction. Makes deep networks trainable.

eli5: Stacking piles of notes together.
simple: Joining maps by stacking their channels; height and width must match.

eli5: Making a picture bigger.
simple: Increasing height and width, here by repeating each value (nearest neighbour).

eli5: Making a picture smaller.
simple: Reducing height and width, usually with a stride-2 conv or pooling.

eli5: Keeps only the strongest value in each small square.
simple: Takes the maximum value in each window; has no learned weights.

eli5: Only half of the notes go through the hard work; the rest skip ahead.
simple: Cross Stage Partial design: split channels, process only part of them, then merge. Saves compute and helps learning.
engineer: Partial feature processing with merge (Wang et al., 2019).

eli5: A block that saves every helper's work and joins it all.
simple: Efficient Layer Aggregation Network: stacks of convs where intermediate outputs are all concatenated.

eli5: A flexible version of ELAN that can use any helper block inside.
simple: Generalized ELAN (YOLOv9): ELAN-style aggregation that can wrap any computational block (e.g. RepNCSP).

eli5: Extra guidance while learning so deep layers do not forget.
simple: Programmable Gradient Information (YOLOv9): auxiliary supervision during training to keep useful information through deep layers.
engineer: Auxiliary reversible branch for gradient reliability.

eli5: Use several branches while learning, then merge them into one for speed.
simple: Training with parallel branches (e.g. 3×3 + 1×1) that are mathematically merged into one conv for inference.
engineer: Linear branch fusion into a single kernel post-training.

eli5: How many times blocks are repeated in a model size.
simple: A scale factor for the number of repeats (n) of each block. Smaller models use fewer repeats.

eli5: How many channels a model size uses.
simple: A scale factor for the number of channels of each layer. Smaller models are narrower.

eli5: The most channels any layer may have in this size.
simple: A cap on channels before the width multiple is applied (e.g. 1024 or 512).
engineer: Upper bound on c before width scaling.

eli5: The model size: nano, small, medium, large, extra-large.
simple: The size variant (n, s, m, l, x) chosen through the depth and width multiples.

eli5: A text recipe that lists the model's layers.
simple: The text file Ultralytics uses to describe a model: one line per layer with [from, repeats, module, args].

eli5: Which earlier layer a layer reads from.
simple: In the YAML, the index of the input layer(s). −1 means 'the previous layer'.
engineer: Input layer indices; negative values are relative.

eli5: Using the finished model on new photos.
simple: Running the trained model to get predictions, as opposed to training it.

eli5: The time when the model learns from labelled photos.
simple: The process of adjusting parameters to reduce the loss on labelled data.
engineer: Optimisation of parameters on a dataset.

eli5: A score for how wrong the model was. Learning tries to make it small.
simple: A number that measures how wrong predictions are; training changes the parameters to make it smaller.
engineer: Differentiable objective minimised by gradient descent.

eli5: Which way to nudge each number to make the model better.
simple: How much the loss changes when a parameter changes; used to update parameters.

eli5: The rule that nudges the numbers while learning.
simple: The algorithm that updates parameters from gradients (SGD, AdamW, MuSGD).

eli5: A kind of thing to find, like 'weed' or 'crop'.
simple: A category the model can predict. nc is the number of classes.
engineer: Label category; nc = number of classes.

eli5: A rectangle drawn around a thing.
simple: A rectangle given by its centre, width and height (or corners) around an object.
engineer: (x, y, w, h) or (x1, y1, x2, y2).

eli5: A box that can turn.
simple: A bounding box with an extra angle, so it can fit tilted objects.

eli5: A special point on a thing, like a knee or a leaf tip.
simple: A labelled point location on an object, with x, y and a visibility value.

eli5: Colouring the exact pixels of each separate thing.
simple: Predicting a pixel mask for each detected object.

eli5: A general shape picture that all objects can mix from.
simple: One of the shared mask bases that are mixed with per-object coefficients to build masks.
engineer: Basis masks for linear mask assembly.

eli5: A way to connect many points together at once, not just in pairs.
simple: A graph where one connection (hyperedge) can link many nodes at once; YOLOv13 uses it to relate many pixels together.
engineer: Generalised graph with edges over vertex sets.

eli5: YOLOv13's part that finds groups of related pixels across map sizes.
simple: Hypergraph-based Adaptive Correlation Enhancement: links pixels from several maps through learned hyperedges and mixes their information.
engineer: Learnable hyperedge construction + linear-complexity hypergraph message passing over multi-scale features.

eli5: YOLOv13's way of handing the shared knowledge to every part of the model.
simple: Full-Pipeline Aggregation-and-Distribution: sends HyperACE features through 'tunnels' into the backbone-neck link, inside the neck, and to the head.

eli5: Storing numbers with fewer digits so the model is smaller and faster.
simple: Using lower-precision numbers (FP16, INT8) for weights and activations to save memory and time, with a small accuracy risk.

eli5: A small computer near the camera, like on a robot or drone.
simple: A low-power device that runs the model on site (for example an NVIDIA Jetson) instead of a big server.

eli5: Starting from a model that already learned from many photos.
simple: Parameters learned on a large dataset (like COCO) used as the start for your own training. Changing the architecture means some weights no longer fit.

eli5: Testing one change at a time to see what really helped.
simple: An experiment that adds or removes one change at a time to measure its effect.

eli5: A big public set of labelled photos with 80 kinds of things.
simple: A standard dataset with 80 classes used to train and compare detectors.

eli5: Making extra practice photos by flipping, cropping and mixing.
simple: Random changes to training images (flips, colour, mosaic) so the model generalises better.

eli5: When some kinds of things appear much more often than others.
simple: When some classes have far more examples than others, so the model may ignore rare ones.

eli5: Cutting a big photo into smaller pieces so tiny things look bigger.
simple: Splitting a large image into overlapping tiles for training/inference so small objects cover more pixels.

eli5: How long the model takes for one photo.
simple: Time per image. Depends on the device, precision, input size and post-processing, so it must be measured on the real hardware.
